headline: High risk: Langflow’s unsandboxed server-side execution and shared state can amplify Dexter’s broad egress into data leakage, cascading errors, and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter can write to .dexter/scratchpad and Langflow can read files and chain agents in graph-based flows, so attacker-controlled content can cross from one agent into the other as trusted input. This is not a proven default direct bridge, but the shared file/workflow surfaces make prompt injection plausible for both agents.
conditions: IF Dexter writes untrusted content into .dexter/scratchpad and Langflow ingests that file in a flow
IF a Langflow flow forwards file contents to another agent node without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the scratchpad from any Langflow-imported directory
Add a provenance tag to every file passed between agents
Disable automatic file-to-prompt ingestion in Langflow flows
Review flow nodes for any instruction-following on raw file content
requires-engineering: add content sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress to multiple APIs; Langflow reads uploaded files and stores per-flow credentials while also using broad egress. Together, sensitive flow inputs or research data can be exposed to external services without a strong isolation boundary, making leakage plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF Dexter processes financial data that is then passed into a Langflow flow
IF Langflow components send uploaded file contents or intermediate outputs to configured external APIs
mitigations: Restrict both agents to a private network egress allowlist
Avoid passing financial data into Langflow unless redacted
Store secrets outside Langflow component stores where possible
Turn off uploads for flows that do not need files
requires-engineering: add DLP and per-flow data classification controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and broad egress, while Langflow supports multiple instances, shared server-side state, and unrestricted filesystem writes with unsandboxed Python components. That creates a direct write/write and state-conflict pathway on shared resources, especially if both operate in the same deployment or workspace.
conditions: IF both agents run against the same filesystem or shared server-side store
IF Langflow Python components write artifacts that Dexter also reads or updates
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate workspace directory
Disable concurrent writes to any shared output path
Serialize runs that touch the same artifacts
Use per-agent service accounts and storage buckets
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is designed to chain multiple agents and tools, so Dexter outputs can become authoritative inputs to downstream actions. Because Dexter performs autonomous execution and Langflow can execute server-side Python and external calls, a mistaken Dexter result can cascade into further automated steps without a verification gate.
conditions: IF a Langflow flow consumes Dexter output as a downstream node input
IF the flow lacks an explicit verification or human approval step before action-taking
mitigations: Insert a validation node before any action node
Require human approval for high-impact flow branches
Log and diff Dexter outputs before reuse
Limit downstream nodes to read-only summarization
requires-engineering: add schema validation and confidence thresholds

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter touches financial data and market data, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and processes uploaded files on server-side infrastructure. If regulated financial or personal data enters Langflow, the pair can create retention, residency, or access-control mismatches; the profiles do not show a compensating compliance boundary, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF regulated financial records or personal data are routed from Dexter into Langflow
IF Langflow retention or hosting location differs from the source-data obligations
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Langflow flows
Redact identifiers before upload
Review retention settings for stored flow inputs and credentials
Document data residency for the deployment
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention enforcement
